intro: Small engine mechanics maintain, repair and troubleshoot machines, skills that many better-paid trades need. The closest of the 25 careers below is engine and machine assembly, with an 85% match, while Industrial Machinery Mechanics are 79% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $64,520, or 35% more.
why_it_works: Fixing mowers, saws and small engines means finding the fault fast, ordering parts and getting customers back to work. O*NET rates equipment maintenance and repairing at 3.88 out of 5 for this job and troubleshooting at 3.75. Industrial machinery, valve and boiler work use the same mechanical skills on bigger systems. Several matches need a certificate. The gaps are installation and supervising people.
tips: Industrial machinery maintenance pays more and often needs only a short certificate.
Control and Valve Installers and Repairers earn $74,340, which is 55% more, and are a 79% match.
Boilermakers earn $76,410, or 60% more, through apprenticeships.

faq.q: What jobs can former small engine mechanics do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Engine and Other Machine Assemblers (85%), electric motor and power tool repairers (83%) and Home Appliance Repairers (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. Electric motor repairers earn $56,210, which is 17% more than the $47,880 small engine mechanic median.

faq.q: Which careers for small engine mechanics pay more?
faq.a: 19 of the 25 matches pay more. Mining roof bolters earn $78,540 (64% more), Boilermakers $76,410 (60% more) and control and valve installers $74,340 (55% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Transportation equipment inspectors earn $92,100 for their broader group.

faq.q: Do small engine mechanics need more education to switch?
faq.a: For some paths. 20 of the 25 matches need no more education than small engine mechanics already have, including 6 of the top 10. A post-secondary certificate is common in close matches, held by 39% of workers in one of them.

faq.q: What skills should small engine mechanics learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are installation, managing people, coordination and operation and control. Operations monitoring already rates 3.38 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so installing larger systems is the main step toward better-paid industrial trades.
